title: change owner: answers 'moved' and notifies the new owner when a readonlyWhen lock kept owner_id unchanged; notified is true whenever emit returns
body:
repo:objectstack#4 · os-project-manager · session_01FEkQ5krBqrrgxCYgjXmfbv

Filing gate ① · Source: fleet · found by the #35270 review sweep (run records r03 M1, r04 S4) on PR #36154, re-read on main c30ce97cd7

## What happens
Change Owner can tell the user a record moved, and tell the named person "a record was assigned to you", when the record did not move. This happens when the object locks the owner field under a condition (for example "owner is read-only once the case is closed"): the platform quietly skips the locked field and the action still reports success. The answer is built from what was asked, not from what was saved. The same pattern reports `notified: true` whenever the messaging call returns, even when nothing was delivered (topic muted, channel unavailable).

- `packages/core/src/security/change-record-owner.ts:302` / `:362`: `engine.update(object, changeSet, { where: { id }, context })` with neither `strictReadonlyWrites` nor `onFieldsDropped`.
- `:306-310` (single) and `:348-357` (bulk): `ownerId` / `queue` copied from the request; any non-throwing update counts as moved.
- The engine strips a caller key that a TRUE `readonlyWhen` locks and answers the stored row (`engine-update.ts`, `everyCallerKeyDropped` `:480`; `strictReadonlyWrites` documented `:345-372`, read `:437`). Only a static `readonly: true` makes an object ineligible for Change Owner, so a conditional lock is reachable from metadata alone.
- Queue target: only `queue` lands, the owner stays, the receipt says `ownerId: null`.
- `notified`: `:259-279` returns `true` after `await messaging.emit(...)` without reading its result; `service-messaging/src/messaging-service.ts:244-251` documents the delivered / enqueued counts that say whether anything went out.

## Done when
- Each owner write passes `strictReadonlyWrites: true` (a stripped `owner_id` / `queue` becomes that row's refusal with its own code), or the written row is compared with the target and a mismatch is a failure.
- `notified` is true only when the emit result reports a delivered or enqueued row.
- Pins: an object with `owner_id.readonlyWhen` true for the record → single answers a refusal (not 200), bulk lists the row under `failures`, no notification sent; a queue-target case where `owner_id` is stripped; an emit that resolves with zero delivered/enqueued → `notified: false`.
- Ablation: drop `strictReadonlyWrites` from the update options and the readonlyWhen pin goes red.

reach: public HTTP doors `POST /api/v1/data/:object/:id/change-owner` and `POST /api/v1/data/:object/change-owner` plus the client's `data.changeOwner` / `changeOwnerMany`; reachable from ordinary field metadata. Read from the code, not measured.
Business reason: users and admins are told ownership changed when it did not, and a colleague is told a record is theirs that is not — work falls through the cracks with no error to notice.
Reader: area:data / domain:server (packages/core security, change-owner).
Dedupe: `change owner`, `owner readonlyWhen`, `notified emit` → #35403, #35399, #35315, #35802 (none carries this); 0 matches for the defect.
Grade: p2 — false success and a false notification on a shipped door, reachable from metadata; no privilege gained.
